The admitted string operations provide equality, concatenation, length and emptiness, but no lexicographic comparison or access to Unicode scalar values.","attempted_representations":["A total list fold can remove duplicate group names using string equality and filtering, but cannot insert or select names in lexicographic order without a string ordering operation.","String length and equality cannot determine lexicographic order for arbitrary distinct strings of equal length. Requiring presorted events or restricting group names would change the specified input domain."]},{"obligation_ids":["O3","O4","O5","O6","I1"],"feature":"Integer-controlled finite sequence generation","reason":"Each established group requires arbitrarily many bucket starts determined by start, end and width, independently of the number of events. The term grammar provides no range construction, integer division, numeric iteration or recursive definitions to generate that sequence.","attempted_representations":["List folds can accumulate records and carry an Option Int previous sum, preserving nulls and zero sums, but they iterate only over existing input lists and cannot visit an arbitrary number of buckets determined by integer fields.","Mapping or filtering events can identify eligible occurrences but cannot generate all empty buckets. Even one out-of-range event can establish a group requiring arbitrarily many empty output records.","A fixed literal list of bucket indices or bounded repeated appends would impose an unsupported bound on the interval. Adding a caller-supplied bucket list would alter the actual input structure."]}]}
